definitions.explanation: A small woodwind instrument shaped like a flute but pitched one octave higher, producing a bright, piercing sound. Common in orchestras and marching bands. From Italian {piccolo} ("small").

examples.japanese: ピッコロ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吹|ふ}く→吹く：02445_fuku⟧。
ピッコロ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦フルート→フルート：04462_furuuto⟧⟦より→より：09476_yori⟧{1|いち}オクターブ⟦{高|たか}い→高い：00500_takai⟧⟦{音|おと}→音：00743_oto⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{出|で}る→出る：00513_deru⟧。
examples.english: The piccolo produces a sound one octave higher than the flute.

examples.japanese: ⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{交響楽団|こうきょうがくだん}→交響楽団：28508_koukyougakudan⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧ピッコロ⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦フルート→フルート：04462_furuuto⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{両方|りょうほう}→両方：01750_ryouhou⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{担当|たんとう}→担当：02567_tantou⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
examples.english: He is in charge of both the piccolo and the flute in the symphony orchestra.

notes:
Loanword from Italian {piccolo} ("small"). In Japanese orchestras the piccolo player is often the second flutist who doubles on piccolo when the score requires it.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ピッコロ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{吹|ふ}く→吹く：02445_fuku⟧: to play the piccolo
- ピッコロ⟦{奏者|そうしゃ}→奏者：06964_sousha⟧: piccolo player
- ピッコロ⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{音色|ねいろ}→音色：07422_neiro⟧: the tone of the piccolo

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ⟦フルート→フルート：04462_furuuto⟧: flute — larger, lower-pitched member of the same family
- ⟦リコーダー→リコーダー：28505_rikoodaa⟧: recorder — a different woodwind, with a fipple mouthpiece, used in schools
